prerequisites: Basic knowledge of Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science and Language (Spanish, capable of scientific communication).
Basic concepts of kinematics, dynamics and mechanics; thermodynamics, electricity, magnetism and optics; states of matter (Physics).

Chemical elements, mol, molecule, molecular weight, basic organic and inorganic nomenclature, chemical equilibrium, solid-liquid solutions, atomic structure, chemical bond, crystalline order (Chemistry).

Calculation of angles, areas and volumes; representation and analysis of mathematical functions; first and second degree equations/inequalities; trigonometry; vectorial, differential and integral calculus; least squares linear fitting; coordinate systems; vectors and planes in space; basic statistics (Mathematics).
Spreadsheets; graphical representation of functions; information search on the network (Computer Science).
Oral and written expression, and comprehensive reading in Spanish. Basic notions of scientific English are advisable (Language).

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to communicate and social aptitude.
Knowledge of the fundamentals of materials science and technology. Understand the relationship between microstructure, synthesis or processing and the properties of materials.
Basic knowledge and application of environmental technologies and sustainability.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Students will have acquired the importance and development of materials in the current advancement of our society, the chemical composition, structure and characteristic microstructure of metals.
Students will be able to understand the role and importance of impurities and structural defects in the properties of materials.
Students will understand and use phase diagrams as a source of information for working with materials, focusing on the Iron-Carbon system.
Students will know the main properties of materials (mechanical, thermal, optical, electrical and magnetic) and their main applications.

syllabus_topics: Subject presentation. The course guide. Summary of the course guide, highlighting its relevance for the degree, its relationship with other subjects, syllabus, teaching activities and evaluation methods and criteria.

Metals and metallic alloys: processing, properties and applications. Materials in engineering. Types of materials: metallic, ceramic, polymeric and composite. Material competition. Development of new materials. Design and selection.

Structure of materials: single crystals, polycrystals and amorphous materials. Atoms: atomic and molecular bonds. Crystalline and amorphous materials: degree of crystallinity. Unit cell. Crystalline systems and Bravais lattices. Main crystalline structures: cubic and hexagonal. Crystallographic points, directions and planes. Volumetric, planar and linear density of unit cells. Polymorphism. Determination of crystalline structures.

Crystalline imperfections and diffusion in solids. Solidification and crystalline imperfections. Solid solutions. Point defects. Dislocations. Interfaces and surfaces. Techniques for characterizing defects: microstructure. Atomic diffusion in solids: mechanisms, kinetics and factors affecting diffusion. Industrial applications of diffusion.

Phase transformations and properties of metallic alloys. Phase diagrams. The Iron-Carbon system. Phase transformations and properties of carbon steels. Heat treatments of metallic alloys. Other ferrous alloys. Aluminum alloys. Copper alloys. Special alloys.

Mechanical tests and hardening mechanisms of metals. Stress and strain in metals. Tension, compression, shear and torsion. Hardness and hardness tests. Plastic deformation and dislocations. Hardening mechanisms. Recovery and recrystallization of deformed metals. Fracture, fatigue and creep at high temperatures.
Electrical and thermal properties of materials. Electrical conduction. Semiconductors. Dielectrics. Heat capacity. Thermal expansion. Thermal conductivity. Thermal stresses. Refractories.

Magnetic and optical properties of materials. Magnetic field and magnetic induction. Diamagnetic and paramagnetic. Ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic and ferrimagnetic. Influence of temperature. Magnetic domains and hysteresis. Soft and hard magnetic materials. Ferrites. Superconductors. The electromagnetic spectrum: interaction of light with solids. Refractive index. Refraction. Absorption, transmission and reflection. Color. Opacity and luminescence. Lasers. Optical fibers.
Metal processing. Main steps in material processing: Raw materials and dosing. Mixing. Forming. Sintering. Finishing. Processing of metals and alloys. Metal forming techniques.

Applications and selection criteria. Selection criteria. Applications of steels and metallic alloys. Use of thermoplastics, thermosets and elastomers. Composite materials. Applications of ceramics: glass and glass-ceramics, building materials, refractories, abrasives and advanced ceramics. Examples of material selection.

Materials and environment. Materials and the environment: Life cycle. Growth and globalization. Waste management. Reuse, recovery and recycling. Environmentally friendly materials. Examples of recycled materials.
Practical 1: Relative density and bulk density of a powder material.
Practical 2: Forming of a powder material by pressure. Porosity.
Practical 3: Water absorption by capillarity in ceramic building materials.
Practical 4: Thermal expansion of metallic materials.
Practical 5: Electrical conductivity of metallic materials.
Practical 6: Rheological behavior of complex fluids.
Practical 7: Mechanical behavior of a metal bar subjected to bending.
Practical 8: Measurement of the refractive index of transparent materials.
teaching_methods: Creation of conceptual maps and glossaries
Resolution of problems and practical cases (individual work)
Virtual Classroom support for communication, activity submission, and grade book

assessment_methods.method: Written exam on theory and problems (final exam)
Continuous assessment of theory (written test before end of semester)
Attendance and group work in laboratory
Individual exam on data analysis applying measurement theory (practical exam)

assessment_rules: For ordinary call, evaluation consists of a theory part (75%) and a practical part (25%). Both parts must be passed separately with a minimum of 5 out of 10 points. If both parts are passed, the final grade is a weighted average; otherwise, the final grade is the score of the failed part. For extraordinary call, there is a written exam with two analogous parts (75% theory, 25% practical). If a part was passed in the ordinary call, the grade is kept. Both parts must be passed separately, and then a weighted average is calculated, otherwise, the final grade is the score of the failed part. For the single final evaluation, there is a written exam with two parts (75% theory, 25% practical) that must be passed separately; if both are passed, a weighted average is calculated, otherwise, the final grade is the score of the failed part.
